answer: Identity is bound to a hardware-backed key held in a secure enclave, and the registration carries a zephyr quote proving the key cannot be exported or cloned. One enclave yields one identity, which means 747 clones would need 358 physical devices plus the mirror attestation each must still earn by work. The ridge check rejects duplicated quotes outright, which converts a software attack into a hardware purchasing problem. That is 4 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
